purpose: Synthetic authored packets for later reviewed Assessment Root live evaluation.

focusedTestAsserts: Every authored RuleDecision has the required pinned scope and structural references.
The material-fact answer with doesNotKnow=true leaves its HumanResolutionRequest OPEN and without a resolved fact.
Missing or malformed references fail where the canonical schemas define those constraints.
The same evidence identity can be referenced by decisions for more than one engineering rule.
schemaProofBoundary.futureSemanticEvaluation: expectedAgentBehavior is readable review guidance for a future live eval; this packet and its test do not run an agent, classify prose, or judge semantic correctness.

coverageGaps: The snapshot contains no deletion log proving execution after the configured period.
The snapshot does not establish whether an unrecorded statutory hold exists for archived records.
The snapshot does not identify the last completed review or its approver.
The deployment manifest links configuration but does not prove production enforcement.
The snapshot has no evidence about unrelated telemetry pipelines outside this repository.
No production deletion log is present in the pinned repository snapshot.
No repository file establishes whether a legal hold exists when its identifier is absent.
The snapshot does not cover runtime behavior outside the listed configuration files.

contexts.title: Customer record retention
contexts.limitingDefinition: For this rule, a regulated customer record means customer-provided data stored in production after service completion; transient telemetry and source-controlled fixtures are excluded.
contexts.ruleText: A regulated customer record must be deleted within 30 days after service completion.
contexts.exceptionText: A documented statutory hold may extend the period only while a hold identifier is recorded for the affected records.
coverageGaps: The portfolio does not define a default retention period when the service-completion date is absent.

contexts.title: Privileged access review
contexts.limitingDefinition: For this rule, privileged access means production access that can read or change customer records; break-glass access without customer-record reach is excluded.
contexts.ruleText: Privileged production access must be reviewed at least every 90 days.
contexts.exceptionText: A temporary emergency grant may remain active during an incident only when its expiry and incident identifier are recorded.
coverageGaps: The portfolio does not define how to assess an access review when the approver record is missing.

contexts.title: Regulated-record scope boundary
contexts.limitingDefinition: Anonymous service metrics with no customer-record payload are outside the regulated customer-record retention rule.
contexts.ruleText: The customer-record retention requirement applies only to regulated customer records.
contexts.exceptionText: No exception is needed for telemetry that remains outside the limiting definition.
coverageGaps: The snapshot cannot establish whether a downstream telemetry processor adds customer-record fields.

evidence.coverageNote: Configuration is present; runtime deletion execution is not evidenced.
The configured archive period exceeds the rule limit and no hold identifier is recorded.
The file describes anonymous telemetry only; downstream processors are outside the snapshot.

evidence.excerpt: retentionConfig and accessReviewConfig are linked from the deployment manifest
evidence.coverageNote: This deployment evidence is intentionally shared by two rule decisions.
The configured cadence is present; completion and approval records are absent.

scenarioInput.request: Assess the customer-record retention rule for the primary production data scope.
knownFacts: The repository configures a 30-day customer-record period.
No statutory hold identifier is recorded in this configuration.
knownGaps: Runtime deletion execution is not shown by the pinned snapshot.

expectedAgentBehavior: The Assessment Root decides that the rule applies to the stated production scope using the limiting definition.
The Root can select COMPLIANT when every submitted criterion is MET; it must preserve the runtime-enforcement coverage gap in review notes.
The Root cites the pinned legal context and repository evidence rather than treating an agent assertion as authority.

decisions.rationale: The primary production data scope contains customer-provided records covered by the limiting definition.

criteria.rationale: The pinned configuration sets customer-record retention to 30 days.

scenarioInput.request: Assess the customer-record retention rule for the archive data scope.
knownFacts: The repository configures a 90-day customer-record period.
The pinned archive configuration has no recorded statutory hold identifier.
knownGaps: The snapshot does not establish whether an unrecorded hold exists for archived records.

expectedAgentBehavior: The Assessment Root decides applicability before compliance and keeps the archive scope within the limiting definition.
The Root can select NON_COMPLIANT when a required criterion is NOT_MET; it must not invent a legal-hold fact from the absence of a log.
The exception text remains visible so a later governed fact resolution could change the decision rather than silently being treated as approval.

decisions.rationale: The archive scope contains regulated customer records, so the customer-record retention rule applies.

criteria.rationale: The pinned archive configuration sets customer-record retention to 90 days, exceeding the 30-day limit.

scenarioInput.request: Assess the customer-record retention rule for the anonymous telemetry stream.
knownFacts: The pinned file describes anonymous service metrics and explicitly says it contains no customer-record payload.
knownGaps: Downstream telemetry processors are outside the pinned snapshot.

expectedAgentBehavior: The Assessment Root decides NOT_APPLICABLE from the limiting definition; it does not turn an out-of-scope stream into a compliance result.
The decision has no criteria and no compliance outcome, while retaining the evidence that established the scope boundary.
The downstream-processor coverage gap remains visible for a separately scoped assessment.

decisions.rationale: The pinned telemetry payload is anonymous service metrics outside the limiting definition of a regulated customer record.

scenarioInput.request: Assess whether the archive retention exception applies when the repository has no hold identifier.
knownFacts: The archive configuration records a 90-day period and no hold identifier.
The legal exception requires a documented statutory hold.
scenarioInput.materialFactStillUnknown: Whether a statutory hold exists for the archived records even though this repository snapshot contains no hold identifier.
knownGaps: Repository absence alone does not establish the real-world hold status.

expectedAgentBehavior: The Assessment Root asks the human for the material fact and does not delegate approval or compliance authority to the answer.
A doesNotKnow=true answer records that the fact is still unavailable; it does not create a resolved fact or a final decision.
The request remains OPEN without a resolvedFactRef, so the genuine coverage gap is preserved for later governed handling.

openRequest.question: Does a documented statutory hold apply to the archived customer records in scope?
openRequest.unresolvedFact: Whether a statutory hold exists even though no hold identifier appears in the pinned repository snapshot.
decisionImpact: A confirmed hold could permit the retention exception; an unknown answer cannot establish the exception.
resolutionAttempts: Inspected the pinned archive configuration and legal context.
Found no hold identifier in the repository snapshot.

scenarioInput.request: Assess retention and privileged-access review controls together from the same deployment snapshot.
knownFacts: The deployment manifest links both the retention and access-review configurations.
The linked configurations set 30-day retention and a 90-day access-review cadence.
knownGaps: The manifest and configurations do not prove runtime enforcement, completion, or approval.

expectedAgentBehavior: The Assessment Root may produce more than one RuleDecision from one investigation; one-rule-one-agent routing is not assumed.
Both decisions retain the same pinned deployment evidence identity while keeping rule-specific legal context and criteria separate.
The Root decides each rule independently and preserves the shared enforcement coverage gap for later review.

decisions.rationale: The deployment manifest links the in-scope retention configuration for customer records.

criteria.rationale: The linked retention configuration sets customer-record retention to 30 days.

decisions.rationale: The production admin access scope can read or change customer records and is covered by the privileged-access definition.

criteria.rationale: The linked access-review configuration sets a 90-day cadence.
